anchors.note: After the top-level zero-sized `mp4a` box is accepted and the sample-entry header is consumed, GPAC enters the audio sample entry child-box parser. The saved run log proves this exact path by reporting `Box "wave" (start 36) has 1 extra bytes` from this function.

This staged tree reaches the `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` arm, not the `GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_UNKNOWN`/`original_4cc` fallback. The nested `esds` already exists under the wave box's child list when this alias is created.

The staged patch replaces this single delete call with explicit unlinking from `ptr->child_boxes` and from each direct child's `child_boxes` before `gf_isom_box_del((GF_Box *)ptr->esd)`, confirming that the missing obligation was to clear every surviving parent-list reference before freeing the old ESDS box.

The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 8` at `/src/gpac/src/isomedia/box_funcs.c:1803:19` in `gf_isom_box_del`, reached from `gf_isom_box_array_reset()` during `gf_isom_delete_movie()`.
The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 8` at `/src/gpac/src/isomedia/box_funcs.c:1803:19` in `gf_isom_box_del`, reached from `gf_isom_box_array_reset()` during `gf_isom_delete_movie()`.

While parsing the witness's nested `esds` box inside the `wave` payload, GPAC allocates a new `GF_ESDBox`. The saved ASan allocation stack identifies this constructor as the heap origin of the object later freed and re-read.

While parsing the registered `wave` box's payload under the outer `mp4a` sample entry, the generic box-array reader creates that wave box's `child_boxes` list and adds the newly parsed ESDS object to it. This is the owning nested-list reference that later survives the free.

The root box header `6d703461` makes `s->type == GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_MP4A` on this path, so in the `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` case the handler chooses `ptr->esd` as the destination field and expects the nested configuration box type to be `esds`. This maps the witness's registered wave child onto the audio entry's ESD slot.

Source. The handler walks the parsed wave box's nested children, finds the `inner_box` whose type matches `ESDS`, and assigns `*cfg_ptr = inner_box`. Because step 3 bound `cfg_ptr` to `ptr->esd`, this aliases `ptr->esd` to the same heap object already stored in the wave box's child list.

On the crashing path `drop_wave` remains false, so the registered `wave` box is not removed from `ptr->child_boxes` and the old ESDS is not moved out of `a->child_boxes`. The aliased object therefore still has its owner-list reference under the nested wave box when control returns.

The normal child-box read does not fail at the `wave` warning itself. Inside `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()`, the byte at file offset `0x38` only makes `to_skip == 1`, logs `Box "wave" (start 36) has 1 extra bytes`, increments `unused_bytes`, and `gf_bs_skip_bytes()` consumes that byte while leaving the `wave` parse successful. Because the outer `mp4a` payload still has eight bytes left at `0x39-0x40`, `gf_isom_box_array_read_ex()` immediately attempts a second child parse from those trailing `0x20` bytes; that all-`0x20` header claims a box larger than the remaining input, so the second `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` returns nonzero. That nonzero `e`, not the warning itself, is why `audio_sample_entry_box_read()` skips `if (!e) return GF_OK;` and falls through to the raw fallback.

The fallback rewinds to `pos`, copies the same 29-byte remaining `mp4a` payload, and scans it for an `esds` header. In the exact witness this copied buffer begins with the 8-byte `wave` header, so when `i == 8` the candidate box starts 8 bytes into the buffer and `data[i+4..i+7]` (offsets 12-15) are `65 73 64 73`; that is the nested `esds` type the loop matches for reparsing.

Root cause call site. Because step 7 matched the nested `esds` header at `i=8` and `ptr->esd` still aliases the old nested box from steps 3-4, the parser asks `gf_isom_box_del_parent()` to delete that box through the audio sample entry's direct `child_boxes` list instead of the nested wave list that still owns it.

This helper only tries to remove `b` from the caller-supplied list and then unconditionally frees it. Here the caller supplied `&ptr->child_boxes`, but the surviving owner list is the nested wave box's `child_boxes`, so freeing `b` leaves that nested list entry dangling.

Later `gf_isom_delete_movie()` recursively destroys top-level boxes. When teardown reaches the registered wave box's nested `child_boxes`, `gf_list_get()` returns the freed old ESDS pointer from step 9 and passes that dangling `a` back into `gf_isom_box_del()`.
Sink. `a` is the dangling pointer retrieved in step 10, so reading `a->child_boxes` dereferences the freed `GF_ESDBox`. AddressSanitizer reports the heap-use-after-free READ 8 at this line.

anchors.note: The registered `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` child path walks the parsed wave box's nested children and aliases the nested `esds` object into `ptr->esd`.

Fallback ESDS reparsing deletes the old aliased `ptr->esd` through the audio sample entry's direct `child_boxes` list even though the registered `wave` child still owns that same object in its nested `child_boxes` list.

AddressSanitizer crash site. During recursive teardown, `a` is the freed old `GF_ESDBox *` still stored in the registered `wave` box's nested `child_boxes` list, so this read dereferences freed heap memory.
